Code 
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))

data_path <- if (file.exists("NYPD_Complaint_Data_2024.csv")) {
  "NYPD_Complaint_Data_2024.csv"
} else {
  "C:/Users/ROG/Downloads/NYPD_Complaint_Data_2024.csv"
}

nypd_raw <- read.csv(
  data_path,
  na.strings = c("", "NA", "(null)"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

retail_places <- c(
  "CHAIN STORE", "DEPARTMENT STORE", "DRUG STORE",
  "GROCERY/BODEGA", "CLOTHING/BOUTIQUE", "FOOD SUPERMARKET",
  "SMALL MERCHANT", "STORE UNCLASSIFIED", "CANDY STORE",
  "LIQUOR STORE", "TELECOMM. STORE", "VARIETY STORE",
  "JEWELRY", "SHOE", "SMOKE SHOP", "BOOK/CARD",
  "VIDEO STORE", "SUPERMARKET"
)

main_crimes <- c(
  "PETIT LARCENY",
  "HARRASSMENT 2",
  "ASSAULT 3 & RELATED OFFENSES",
  "GRAND LARCENY",
  "CRIMINAL MISCHIEF & RELATED OF"
)

day_levels <- c(
  "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday",
  "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"
)

borough_levels <- c(
  "BRONX", "BROOKLYN", "MANHATTAN", "QUEENS", "STATEN ISLAND"
)

day_lookup <- c(
  "Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday",
  "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday"
)

nypd_clean <- nypd_raw %>%
  mutate(
    complaint_date = as.Date(CMPLNT_FR_DT, format = "%m/%d/%Y"),
    hour = as.numeric(substr(CMPLNT_FR_TM, 1, 2)),
    day_of_week = day_lookup[as.POSIXlt(complaint_date)$wday + 1],
    day_of_week = factor(day_of_week, levels = day_levels),
    retail_group = case_when(
      PREM_TYP_DESC %in% retail_places ~ "Retail",
      !is.na(PREM_TYP_DESC) ~ "Non-retail",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    crime_group = case_when(
      OFNS_DESC %in% main_crimes ~ OFNS_DESC,
      !is.na(OFNS_DESC) ~ "Other offenses",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    petit_larceny = case_when(
      OFNS_DESC == "PETIT LARCENY" ~ "Petit larceny",
      !is.na(OFNS_DESC) ~ "Other offenses",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(PREM_TYP_DESC),
    !is.na(OFNS_DESC),
    !is.na(retail_group),
    !is.na(petit_larceny),
    !is.na(hour),
    !is.na(complaint_date),
    hour >= 0,
    hour <= 23
  )

fmt_n <- function(x) scales::comma(x)
fmt_pct <- function(x, accuracy = 0.1) {
  scales::percent(x, accuracy = accuracy)
}

start_date <- min(nypd_clean$complaint_date)
end_date <- max(nypd_clean$complaint_date)
clean_total <- nrow(nypd_clean)

summary_table <- nypd_clean %>%
  count(retail_group, petit_larceny) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = petit_larceny,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Total = `Petit larceny` + `Other offenses`,
    Proportion = `Petit larceny` / Total
  )

retail_petit <- summary_table %>%
  filter(retail_group == "Retail") %>%
  pull(`Petit larceny`)
retail_total <- summary_table %>%
  filter(retail_group == "Retail") %>%
  pull(Total)
nonretail_petit <- summary_table %>%
  filter(retail_group == "Non-retail") %>%
  pull(`Petit larceny`)
nonretail_total <- summary_table %>%
  filter(retail_group == "Non-retail") %>%
  pull(Total)

retail_prop <- retail_petit / retail_total
nonretail_prop <- nonretail_petit / nonretail_total
prop_gap <- retail_prop - nonretail_prop
alpha <- 0.05
se_null <- sqrt(nonretail_prop * (1 - nonretail_prop) / retail_total)
z_stat <- (retail_prop - nonretail_prop) / se_null
p_value <- pnorm(z_stat, lower.tail = FALSE)
p_value_text <- if_else(p_value < 0.001, "< 0.001", as.character(round(p_value, 3)))

expected_petit_null <- retail_total * nonretail_prop
expected_other_null <- retail_total - expected_petit_null

hatpc_hypotheses <- tibble(
  Hypothesis = c("H₀", "H₁"),
  Statement = c(
    paste0(
      "Retail petit larceny complaint proportion = non-retail baseline (",
      fmt_pct(nonretail_prop), ")"
    ),
    paste0(
      "Retail petit larceny complaint proportion > non-retail baseline (",
      fmt_pct(nonretail_prop), ")"
    )
  ),
  Meaning_for_client = c(
    "Retail premises do not show a higher petit larceny complaint proportion than the non-retail comparison group.",
    "Retail premises show a higher petit larceny complaint proportion, supporting a retail-specific response."
  )
)

hatpc_assumptions <- tibble(
  Assumption = c(
    "Binary outcome",
    "Large-count normal approximation",
    "Approximate independence",
    "Measurement in context"
  ),
  Check = c(
    "Each complaint is grouped as petit larceny or other offences.",
    paste0(
      "n×p₀ = ", fmt_n(round(expected_petit_null)),
      " and n×(1-p₀) = ", fmt_n(round(expected_other_null)),
      ", both above 10."
    ),
    "Each row is treated as one complaint record, although repeated stores or areas may appear.",
    "The analysis uses NYPD complaint categories as recorded in the dataset."
  ),
  Implication = c(
    "A proportion test is suitable.",
    "The z approximation is reasonable.",
    "This is a limitation, so the result should guide a pilot rather than a permanent policy alone.",
    "The result concerns recorded complaints, not every actual crime."
  )
)

hatpc_calc <- tibble(
  Step = c(
    "Retail observed proportion",
    "Non-retail baseline proportion",
    "Expected petit larceny count under H₀",
    "Expected other-offence count under H₀",
    "Standard error",
    "z statistic",
    "p-value"
  ),
  Working = c(
    paste0(fmt_n(retail_petit), " / ", fmt_n(retail_total)),
    paste0(fmt_n(nonretail_petit), " / ", fmt_n(nonretail_total)),
    paste0(fmt_n(retail_total), " × ", fmt_pct(nonretail_prop)),
    paste0(fmt_n(retail_total), " - ", fmt_n(round(expected_petit_null))),
    "√(p₀ × (1 - p₀) / n)",
    "(p̂ - p₀) / SE",
    "P(Z ≥ z)"
  ),
  Result = c(
    fmt_pct(retail_prop),
    fmt_pct(nonretail_prop),
    fmt_n(round(expected_petit_null)),
    fmt_n(round(expected_other_null)),
    round(se_null, 5),
    round(z_stat, 2),
    p_value_text
  )
)

observed_expected_table <- tibble(
  `Complaint type` = c("Petit larceny", "Other offences"),
  `Observed retail count` = c(retail_petit, retail_total - retail_petit),
  `Expected under H₀` = c(expected_petit_null, expected_other_null)
) %>%
  mutate(
    Difference = `Observed retail count` - `Expected under H₀`,
    `Observed retail count` = fmt_n(round(`Observed retail count`)),
    `Expected under H₀` = fmt_n(round(`Expected under H₀`)),
    Difference = fmt_n(round(Difference))
  )

p_value_table <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Question answered by the p-value",
    "Observed test statistic",
    "Observed p-value",
    "Comparison with alpha",
    "Meaning before the final conclusion"
  ),
  Interpretation = c(
    "If H₀ were true, how unusual would it be to observe a retail petit larceny proportion at least this high?",
    paste0("z = ", round(z_stat, 2), ", one-sided p ", p_value_text),
    paste0("p ", p_value_text),
    paste0("p ", p_value_text, " is below the significance level α = ", alpha),
    "The retail complaint pattern is far above the non-retail baseline. The formal decision is stated in the conclusion."
  )
)

stat_summary <- tibble(
  Measure = c(
    "Retail complaints recorded as petit larceny",
    "Non-retail baseline",
    "Difference in proportions",
    "Significance level",
    "One-sample proportion test"
  ),
  Result = c(
    paste0(fmt_n(retail_petit), " / ", fmt_n(retail_total), " (", fmt_pct(retail_prop), ")"),
    paste0(fmt_n(nonretail_petit), " / ", fmt_n(nonretail_total), " (", fmt_pct(nonretail_prop), ")"),
    paste0(fmt_pct(prop_gap), " percentage points higher in retail premises"),
    paste0("α = ", alpha),
    paste0("z = ", round(z_stat, 2), ", p ", p_value_text)
  )
)

main_premises <- c(
  "CHAIN STORE", "DEPARTMENT STORE", "DRUG STORE",
  "GROCERY/BODEGA", "CLOTHING/BOUTIQUE", "STREET",
  "RESIDENCE - APT. HOUSE", "RESIDENCE-HOUSE",
  "RESIDENCE - PUBLIC HOUSING", "TRANSIT - NYC SUBWAY"
)

fig1_data <- nypd_clean %>%
  mutate(
    premise_for_plot = case_when(
      PREM_TYP_DESC %in% main_premises ~ PREM_TYP_DESC,
      TRUE ~ "Other premises"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(premise_for_plot, crime_group) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(premise_for_plot) %>%
  mutate(
    total_complaints = sum(count),
    proportion = count / total_complaints,
    petit_larceny_prop = sum(count[crime_group == "PETIT LARCENY"]) / total_complaints
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

fig1_order <- fig1_data %>%
  distinct(premise_for_plot, petit_larceny_prop) %>%
  arrange(desc(petit_larceny_prop)) %>%
  pull(premise_for_plot)

fig1_data <- fig1_data %>%
  mutate(
    premise_for_plot = factor(premise_for_plot, levels = fig1_order)
  )

fig1_labels <- fig1_data %>%
  distinct(premise_for_plot, total_complaints)

premise_summary <- nypd_clean %>%
  group_by(PREM_TYP_DESC) %>%
  summarise(
    total_complaints = n(),
    petit_larceny_count = sum(petit_larceny == "Petit larceny"),
    petit_larceny_prop = petit_larceny_count / total_complaints,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    premise_group = if_else(PREM_TYP_DESC %in% retail_places, "Retail", "Non-retail")
  )

top5_retail_names <- nypd_clean %>%
  filter(PREM_TYP_DESC %in% retail_places) %>%
  count(PREM_TYP_DESC, name = "total_complaints") %>%
  arrange(desc(total_complaints)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  pull(PREM_TYP_DESC)

fig2_premise_order <- nypd_clean %>%
  filter(PREM_TYP_DESC %in% top5_retail_names) %>%
  group_by(PREM_TYP_DESC) %>%
  summarise(
    total_complaints = n(),
    petit_larceny_count = sum(petit_larceny == "Petit larceny"),
    petit_larceny_prop = petit_larceny_count / total_complaints,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(petit_larceny_prop)) %>%
  pull(PREM_TYP_DESC)

fig2_data <- nypd_clean %>%
  filter(
    PREM_TYP_DESC %in% top5_retail_names,
    !is.na(BORO_NM),
    BORO_NM != "(null)"
  ) %>%
  group_by(BORO_NM, PREM_TYP_DESC) %>%
  summarise(
    total_complaints = n(),
    petit_larceny_count = sum(petit_larceny == "Petit larceny"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    petit_larceny_prop = petit_larceny_count / total_complaints,
    PREM_TYP_DESC = factor(
      PREM_TYP_DESC,
      levels = rev(fig2_premise_order)
    ),
    BORO_NM = factor(
      BORO_NM,
      levels = borough_levels
    )
  )

if (!requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("The jsonlite package is needed to draw the borough map.")
}

borough_geo <- jsonlite::fromJSON(borough_geo_path, simplifyVector = FALSE)

get_borough_name <- function(properties) {
  toupper(properties$boroname)
}

flatten_borough_feature <- function(feature, feature_id) {
  borough_name <- get_borough_name(feature$properties)
  coordinates <- feature$geometry$coordinates

  if (feature$geometry$type == "Polygon") {
    coordinates <- list(coordinates)
  }

  purrr::imap_dfr(coordinates, function(polygon, polygon_id) {
    purrr::imap_dfr(polygon, function(ring, ring_id) {
      tibble(
        long = purrr::map_dbl(ring, 1),
        lat = purrr::map_dbl(ring, 2),
        group = paste(feature_id, polygon_id, ring_id, sep = "-"),
        BORO_NM = borough_name
      )
    })
  })
}

borough_shapes <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  borough_geo$features,
  flatten_borough_feature
) %>%
  mutate(BORO_NM = factor(BORO_NM, levels = borough_levels))

fig2_map_counts <- nypd_clean %>%
  filter(
    retail_group == "Retail",
    petit_larceny == "Petit larceny",
    !is.na(BORO_NM),
    BORO_NM != "(null)"
  ) %>%
  count(BORO_NM, name = "retail_petit_larceny_complaints")

fig2_map_data <- borough_shapes %>%
  left_join(fig2_map_counts, by = "BORO_NM") %>%
  mutate(
    retail_petit_larceny_complaints = replace_na(
      retail_petit_larceny_complaints,
      0
    )
  )

fig2_map_labels <- fig2_map_data %>%
  group_by(BORO_NM) %>%
  summarise(
    long = mean(range(long)),
    lat = mean(range(lat)),
    retail_petit_larceny_complaints = first(retail_petit_larceny_complaints),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    label = paste0(
      stringr::str_to_title(as.character(BORO_NM)),
      "\n",
      fmt_n(retail_petit_larceny_complaints)
    )
  )

fig3_data <- nypd_clean %>%
  filter(
    PREM_TYP_DESC %in% top5_retail_names,

  ) %>%
  count(PREM_TYP_DESC, hour, name = "reported_complaints") %>%
  complete(
    PREM_TYP_DESC = top5_retail_names,
    hour = 0:23,
    fill = list(reported_complaints = 0)
  )

fig3_peaks <- fig3_data %>%
  group_by(PREM_TYP_DESC) %>%
  slice_max(reported_complaints, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

peak_hour <- function(premise) {
  hour_value <- fig3_peaks %>%
    filter(PREM_TYP_DESC == premise) %>%
    pull(hour)

  if (length(hour_value) == 0) {
    NA_integer_
  } else {
    hour_value[1]
  }
}

fig3_heatmap_data <- nypd_clean %>%
  filter(
    retail_group == "Retail",
    petit_larceny == "Petit larceny"
  ) %>%
  count(day_of_week, hour, name = "reported_complaints") %>%
  complete(
    day_of_week = factor(day_levels, levels = day_levels),
    hour = 0:23,
    fill = list(reported_complaints = 0)
  )

report_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +

    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

offense_colours <- c(
  "PETIT LARCENY" = "#4C78A8",
  "HARRASSMENT 2" = "#F58518",
  "ASSAULT 3 & RELATED OFFENSES" = "#E45756",
  "GRAND LARCENY" = "#72B7B2",

  "Other offenses" = "#B8B8B8"
)

Client Bio

Kenny Minaya

Client: Commissioner, New York City Small Business Services (SBS; NYC SBS, 2026).

SBS supports small businesses and commercial districts, so he can support merchant outreach and BID/NYPD coordination around retail theft.

  1. NYC SBS profile.
  2. Image: Bronx Times.

Recommendation

  1. Run a 90-day Retail Theft Support Sprint for drug stores, chain stores and department stores.

  2. Start in Manhattan, Queens and Brooklyn through merchant visits, BID coordination and NYPD referral contacts.

  3. Focus support during premise-specific peak hours, then use complaint trends and retailer feedback to decide expansion.

Evidence

This analysis uses NYPD Complaint Data Historic (NYC Open Data, 2025) and NYC retail-theft policy evidence involving SBS (NYC Office of the Mayor, 2023b). After cleaning key fields, I analyse 136,022 recorded complaints from 2024-10-01 to 2024-12-31. To support the recommended Retail Theft Support Sprint, I compare petit larceny complaint patterns by premise type, borough and hour. Each row is a complaint record, so the evidence describes reported demand, not every actual offence.

ggplot(

  aes(
    x = forcats::fct_rev(premise_for_plot),

  )
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.78) +

      x = forcats::fct_rev(premise_for_plot),
      y = 1.03,
      label = fmt_n(total_complaints)
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 0,
    size = 3
  ) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
    limits = c(0, 1.16)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = offense_colours) +
  labs(
    title = "Offence Profiles Differ Across Premise Types",
    subtitle = "Premise types are ordered by the proportion recorded as petit larceny",
    x = "Premise type",
    y = "Proportion of NYPD crime complaints",
    fill = "Offence description"
  ) +
  report_theme +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.margin = margin(5.5, 48, 5.5, 5.5)
  )

Figure 1 shows that premise type and offence mix are linked. Petit larceny is much more visible in retail premises than in streets, residences or subways. This means SBS should focus on retail premises first, not all premise types.

Code 
knitr::kable(
  stat_summary,
  caption = "Statistical summary for the retail focus",
  align = c("l", "l")
)
Statistical summary for the retail focus
Measure Result
Retail complaints recorded as petit larceny 12,619 / 18,743 (67.3%)
Non-retail baseline 14,092 / 117,279 (12.0%)
Difference in proportions 55.3% percentage points higher in retail premises
Significance level α = 0.05
One-sample proportion test z = 232.89, p < 0.001

The statistical summary formalises this pattern: 67.3% of retail-premise complaints were petit larceny, compared with 12.0% for non-retail complaints. The one-sample proportion test gives p < 0.001, below 0.05, supporting a retail-focused response while not proving causation.

  scale_x_continuous(

    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(day_levels)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#EEF5FB",
    high = "#08519C",
    name = "Reported\ncomplaints"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Retail Petit Larceny Complaints Are Concentrated by Time",
    subtitle = "Darker cells show more reported complaints",
    x = "Hour of occurrence",
    y = "Day of week"
  ) +
  report_theme +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

Figure 3A: Retail petit larceny complaints by hour and day of week.

Code 
ggplot(
  fig3_data,
  aes(
    x = hour,
    y = reported_complaints,
    color = PREM_TYP_DESC,
    group = PREM_TYP_DESC
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 2)) +
  labs(
    title = "Retail Petit Larceny Complaints Rise During Trading Hours",
    subtitle = "Lines show the five retail premise types with the largest total complaint volume",
    x = "Hour of occurrence",
    y = "Number of NYPD crime complaints",
    color = "Retail premise type"
  ) +
  report_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Figure 3B: Hourly retail petit larceny complaints for the five retail premise types with the largest total complaint counts.

Together, Figure 3A and Figure 3B show late-morning to early-evening concentration, but not one universal peak. Drug stores peak at 9:00, chain stores at 14:00, department stores and clothing/boutiques at 16:00, and grocery/bodegas at 17:00. This supports premise-specific outreach during trading hours, consistent with shoplifting and retail-security evidence (ASU POP Center, n.d.; SDM, 2024).

Limitations

  1. Complaint records, not all crimes: NYPD data include only reported or recorded incidents. Underreporting means results show agency-visible demand, not all theft (RILA, 2025).

  2. Time period: the data cover only the last three months of 2024, so holiday shopping or policing patterns may affect results.

  3. Missing foot traffic: without visitor counts, borough exposure, sales or opening hours, high complaints may reflect exposure rather than higher risk per visitor. The sprint should collect these before expansion.

Ethics Statement

I followed professional competence by checking variable meanings and stating that counts are complaints. I followed respect by reporting group patterns without blaming individual people, workers, customers or communities (International Statistical Institute, n.d.).

Appendix: HATPC

This appendix records the full HATPC process for the hypothesis test used in the Evidence section. The test asks whether retail-premise NYPD complaints have a higher petit larceny proportion than the non-retail baseline. It is a comparison of recorded complaint proportions, not a test of whether retail premises cause petit larceny.

H: Hypotheses

Let p be the true proportion of retail-premise complaints recorded as petit larceny. The comparison value is the non-retail baseline: 12.0% of non-retail complaints in this dataset were recorded as petit larceny. This baseline is useful because it comes from the same NYPD dataset and the same cleaned time period.

Code 
knitr::kable(
  hatpc_hypotheses,
  caption = "Null and alternative hypotheses",
  align = c("l", "l", "l")
)
Null and alternative hypotheses
Hypothesis Statement Meaning_for_client
H₀ Retail petit larceny complaint proportion = non-retail baseline (12.0%) Retail premises do not show a higher petit larceny complaint proportion than the non-retail comparison group.
H₁ Retail petit larceny complaint proportion > non-retail baseline (12.0%) Retail premises show a higher petit larceny complaint proportion, supporting a retail-specific response.

The alternative hypothesis is one-sided because the recommendation only needs evidence that retail premises are higher than the non-retail comparison group.

A: Assumptions

Code 
knitr::kable(
  hatpc_assumptions,
  caption = "Assumptions and checks",
  align = c("l", "l", "l")
)
Assumptions and checks
Assumption Check Implication
Binary outcome Each complaint is grouped as petit larceny or other offences. A proportion test is suitable.
Large-count normal approximation n×p₀ = 2,252 and n×(1-p₀) = 16,491, both above 10. The z approximation is reasonable.
Approximate independence Each row is treated as one complaint record, although repeated stores or areas may appear. This is a limitation, so the result should guide a pilot rather than a permanent policy alone.
Measurement in context The analysis uses NYPD complaint categories as recorded in the dataset. The result concerns recorded complaints, not every actual crime.

The weakest assumption is independence, because the dataset may include repeated complaints from similar stores or areas. For this reason, the test is used as evidence for a targeted pilot, not as proof of causation or as proof that the pattern will hold in every future period.

T: Test Statistic

This is a one-sample proportion test with significance level α = 0.05.

z = (p̂ - p₀) / √(p₀ × (1 - p₀) / n)

Using p̂ = 67.3%, the non-retail baseline p₀ = 12.0%, n = 18,743, and SE = 0.00237:

SE = √(p₀ × (1 - p₀) / n) = 0.00237

z = (p̂ - p₀) / SE = (0.673 - 0.12) / 0.00237

z = 232.89

Code 
knitr::kable(
  hatpc_calc,
  caption = "Step-by-step test calculation",
  align = c("l", "l", "l")
)
Step-by-step test calculation
Step Working Result
Retail observed proportion 12,619 / 18,743 67.3%
Non-retail baseline proportion 14,092 / 117,279 12.0%
Expected petit larceny count under H₀ 18,743 × 12.0% 2,252
Expected other-offence count under H₀ 18,743 - 2,252 16,491
Standard error √(p₀ × (1 - p₀) / n) 0.00237
z statistic (p̂ - p₀) / SE 232.89
p-value P(Z ≥ z) < 0.001
Code 
knitr::kable(
  observed_expected_table,
  caption = "Observed retail counts compared with expected counts under H₀",
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r")
)
Observed retail counts compared with expected counts under H₀
Complaint type Observed retail count Expected under H₀ Difference
Petit larceny 12,619 2,252 10,367
Other offences 6,124 16,491 -10,367

Under H₀, retail premises would be expected to follow the non-retail petit larceny proportion. The observed retail petit larceny count is much higher than the expected count under that baseline, producing a large positive z statistic.

P: P-value

The p-value is not the probability that H₀ is true. It is the probability of seeing a result at least as extreme as this one if retail premises really followed the non-retail baseline. Therefore, a very small p-value means the observed retail pattern is difficult to explain as ordinary random variation around the baseline.

Code 
knitr::kable(
  p_value_table,
  caption = "P-value interpretation before the conclusion",
  align = c("l", "l")
)
P-value interpretation before the conclusion
Item Interpretation
Question answered by the p-value If H₀ were true, how unusual would it be to observe a retail petit larceny proportion at least this high?
Observed test statistic z = 232.89, one-sided p < 0.001
Observed p-value p < 0.001
Comparison with alpha p < 0.001 is below the significance level α = 0.05
Meaning before the final conclusion The retail complaint pattern is far above the non-retail baseline. The formal decision is stated in the conclusion.

The one-sided p-value is < 0.001, which is far below the significance level of 0.05. This means the formal decision should be made in favour of the alternative hypothesis.

C: Conclusion

Statistical conclusion: Since the one-sided p-value is < 0.001, which is below α = 0.05, I reject H₀ and keep H₁ as the better-supported explanation. There is strong statistical evidence that retail-premise complaints have a higher petit larceny proportion than the non-retail baseline.

Scientific conclusion: In context, this supports a targeted retail theft support sprint rather than a general, untargeted crime response. The hypothesis test supports the retail focus; the descriptive figures guide borough and timing priorities. Because the test uses recorded complaints, it should guide the pilot, not explain all retail theft.
